description: Eval set for dictation cleanup prompt optimization. Inputs simulate raw dictation app output (partial punctuation, capitalization attempts, filler words, thought drifts). Expected outputs preserve meaning and content exactly while fixing structure (punctuation, grammar, formatting). Speaker's phrasing, reasoning, and voice are kept intact. Only pure filler words are removed. Captures are always trailing the dictated text (separated by \n\n), matching the app's Mode.applyPreProcessing() behavior.

evals.input: so the way the caching layer works is basically. you have your primary cache which is Redis and then behind that you have a secondary cache which is just in memory on each node. And when a request comes in it first checks the local cache and if it's not there it goes to Redis and if it's not in Redis either then it hits the database. The tricky part is invalidation because you have to invalidate both layers. and if you only invalidate Redis but not the local cache you get stale data for up to like 30 seconds which is the TTL on the local cache. We had a bug with this last month actually where. where prices were showing wrong for some users because of exactly this issue
evals.expected_output: So the way the caching layer works is basically: you have your primary cache, which is Redis, and then behind that you have a secondary cache, which is just in-memory on each node. And when a request comes in, it first checks the local cache, and if it's not there, it goes to Redis, and if it's not in Redis either, then it hits the database. The tricky part is invalidation, because you have to invalidate both layers. And if you only invalidate Redis but not the local cache, you get stale data for up to 30 seconds, which is the TTL on the local cache. We had a bug with this last month actually, where prices were showing wrong for some users because of exactly this issue.

evals.expected_output: So my grandmother used to make this amazing soup, and I've been trying to recreate it for years. The base is pretty simple — it's just onions, carrots, celery, the usual.
